correctness.rationale: The centre-feasibility lemma is an if-and-only-if argument for every possible leaf-answer pattern and every hub-answer pattern. The case classification is exhaustive for colour palette size three and accounts for all selected/unselected hubs. The generating polynomial follows by exact target-palette counts. Degree and highest coefficient follow by all-vertex obstruction plus explicit support witnesses and counting the one omitted vertex. Reconstruction is a strict integer monotonicity argument. The embedded standalone Python checker agreed with 256256 full-support traces, centre feasibility decisions and all polynomial coefficients on eleven trees, plus 121 arithmetic checks. Finite checks are corroboration, not proof of unbounded assertions.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The vertex projection is a Boolean existential image of the full query-support family and loses mark multiplicities. On the three-vertex support consisting of both pendant leaves and one hub of a four-vertex double star, both leaves queried for colour one and the hub queried for colour two are shattered, whereas marking that hub for colour one is not even all-positive realizable. originality.rationale: A known double-star result only classifies vertex-projected supports and the VC dimension; the new formula counts every individual colour-marked support. The projection does not determine these multiplicities. The nearest published full-query polynomial is for complete bipartite graphs, a different and strictly more restrictive proper-colouring family. General 2017–2022 primary literature supplies definitions and a learning context but not this coefficient formula. Specific equivalence, stronger-coverage and exact-database searches were performed; unindexed synonym-based priority risk remains.

value.rationale: Unlike the known vertex projection, this natural invariant counts each individual named-colour Boolean query support and describes every rank across an infinite two-parameter tree family. Its top coefficient at known graph order recovers the unordered double-star branch sizes, detecting structure despite identical scalar VC dimension. The formula and reconstruction are not merely a change of variables from the old vertex-support count.
